text:
Jin Park: heads up - we just got a support escalation from Acme about big p95/p99 latency regressions on generation.v1 in us-west1. customer sees p95 jump ~180ms -> ~420ms for long-context jobs (~1k tokens). they attached traces and a repro curl.

Samir Gupta: thanks. which model variant and pool?

Jin Park: rw1-13b-fp16 on dedicated pool d-prod-usw-3. Affects both hosted and dedicated for that model when seq_len >= 768. rate is low but spikes kill SLA.

Eliot Rivera: I see a spike in our latency dashboard around 2230011200 correlating with a runtime rollout. we turned on the new kernel selector that prefers FlashAttention v2 for compatible arches. commit: abcdef1 (runtime: kernel-selection: prefer-flashattn).

Maria Chen: rolling that back immediately might be safest. I can reproduce locally with a small loadtest. gave a quick repro:

```bash
# repro (single host):
export ENABLE_FLASHATTN=1
./perf-client --model rw1-13b-fp16 --seq 1024 --batch 1 --iter 200 --host http://10.0.0.5:8080

# compare toggles:
export ENABLE_FLASHATTN=0 # fallback to SDPA
./perf-client --same-args
```

Maria Chen: with ENABLE_FLASHATTN=1 p95 ~= 420ms, p99 ~ 1.1s. with ENABLE_FLASHATTN=0 p95 ~= 175ms, p99 ~ 320ms. same binary, same kernel build, only runtime toggle changed.

Samir Gupta: interesting. Could be a specific combination of compile flags + kernel selection causing a bad codepath. Did we change compiler flags in the last build?

Eliot Rivera: yes — we rebuilt kernels with extra vectorization flags to optimize SDPA -> COMPILE_FLAGS="-O3 -march=znver2 -ffast-math" but that should not affect flashattn lower-level code. however the selector now picks a different kernel for >512 seq.

Jin Park: ops-bot fired an alert when customer open ticket #6789 escalated to P1.

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2230 - p95 regression for rw1-13b-fp16 in us-west1. Pinged oncall.

Maria Chen: quick root-cause hypothesis: the FlashAttention v2 kernel we enabled has a fallback path for certain batch/seq combos that hits a slow path (mutex contention in kv-cache or suboptimal launches). I saw lock contention traces in the perf-client. snippet:

```
# from perf logs
FlashAttnKernel::execute() waiting on mutex 0x7f9a2f...  23ms
KVCache::write() contended for 12ms
```

Maria Chen: repro steps I pushed to our test harness:
1) pull runtime image with abcdef1
2) run 5 hosts with ENABLE_FLASHATTN=1 and 5 with =0
3) run seq=1024 load at 2 qps each, B=1
4) observe p95/p99 divergence in 10-30s

Samir Gupta: thanks. can you post the minimal diff so I can try a local quick-fix? if it's mutex we might be able to avoid the slow path by relaxing a condition or forcing a different kernel launch shape.

Maria Chen: minimal workaround: set KERNEL_SELECTOR=prefer_sdpa (runtime config) or ENABLE_FLASHATTN=0. I tested a 10% canary change to prefer_sdpa and it eliminated the p95 regression for those hosts.

Eliot Rivera: ops plan:
- immediate: roll flashattn preference back in us-west1 by changing runtime config to prefer_sdpa for rw1-13b-fp16 (canary -> 100% over 15min). assigned to Samir.
- short-term: pin kernel selection for heavy-context models and add metric alert for mutex wait time > 5ms. assigned to Maria.
- long-term: add unit perf tests for seq>=512 across kernels and add selector A/B testing harness. assigned to Jin.

Samir Gupta: I'm doing the rollback now:
```bash
# update config for pool d-prod-usw-3
redwoodctl pools update d-prod-usw-3 --set "kernel_selector=prefer_sdpa" --models rw1-13b-fp16 --canary 0.1
```
Applying to 10% hosts now. will monitor.

ops-bot: Config change started: pool=d-prod-usw-3, model=rw1-13b-fp16, kernel_selector=prefer_sdpa, canary=10%

Jin Park: monitoring dashboards show p95 for the canary hosts falling back to ~170ms within 4 minutes. good signal.

Eliot Rivera: recommend we keep canary running at 10% for 30m, then promote to 100% if stable. Also we should notify Acme support with mitigation and ETA for permanent fix.

Samir Gupta: I'll open a PR to revert commit abcdef1 and add a feature-flag guard so kernel-selector change requires perf-safety opt-in. PR: https://git.internal/rw/runtime/pull/4021

Maria Chen: adding perf traces and a small synthetic that reproduces the mutex contention to the CI perf suite. will link tests in PR.

Jin Park: I'll update the support ticket with the mitigation and timeline.

Eliot Rivera: postmortem action items:
- revert runtime commit if PR doesn't land in 48h
- add selector telemetry (per-kernel latency by seq/batch)
- add rollout guardrails for kernel selection changes

Samir Gupta: can confirm canary -> 100% has completed. p95 back to normal across pool. rolling change to secondary regions next.

Jin Park: closing loop with customer: sent update and temporary mitigation. they acknowledged and will re-open if they see further issues. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Incident INC-2230 resolved (mitigated). Links: ticket#6789, PR#4021.

Eliot Rivera: nice quick response team. let's keep the perf tests and selector guards a priority this sprint.

Maria Chen: filing follow-up RFC for kernel-selector lifecycle and compile-flag hygiene.

Samir Gupta: thanks all.
